title: Supercuspidal Datum
body_html:
Supercuspidal Datum

For a classical group \(G=U(V)\), a supercuspidal datum is a tuple \[ \Sigma=(x,\Gamma,\phi,\rho) \] with the following structure.

  • \(\Gamma\in\mathbf g\) is tamely ramified semisimple and admits a good factorization compatible with \(G^0=Z_G(\Gamma)\).
  • The center of the connected component of \(G^0\) is anisotropic.
  • \(x\) is a vertex in the building \(B(G^0)\), so the connected component of \(G_x^0\) is a maximal parahoric subgroup.
  • \(\phi:G_x^0\to\mathbb C^\times\) is a character whose restriction to the pro-unipotent radical agrees with the character determined by \(\Gamma\).
  • \(\rho\) is an irreducible cuspidal representation of the finite reductive quotient \(G_x^0/G_{x,0+}^0\).

The depth of \(\Sigma\) is \[ \operatorname{depth}(\Sigma)=\max\{\operatorname{depth}(\Gamma),0\}. \] If the same tuple satisfies the conditions except that \(\rho\) is merely irreducible, it is a refined \(K\)-type datum rather than a supercuspidal datum.
